summary: Configured VyOS (node1) as router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.1.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.2.0/24 via eth2). Applied a default-drop forward filter with established/related accepted and one explicit-allow rule for TCP/5432 from eth1→eth2 (node2→node3). Verified node2 can reach node3:5432 while ping and all other ports/directions between the LANs are rejected. Also opened tcp/5432 in node3's local firewalld (host-level default deny) so the allowed flow actually reaches the service. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, and node3: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state on each, rebooted each node individually, polled until exec access returned, confirmed a changed boot_id, and re-verified config persistence and identical firewall/connectivity behavior after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (VyOS 2026.04 rolling) interfaces eth0/eth1/eth2 and node2/node3 (RHEL7.9) interfaces eth0/eth1
Assigned node1 eth1=10.50.1.254/24 (lan-a) and eth2=10.50.2.254/24 (lan-b) via VyOS configure/commit/save
Assigned node2 eth1=10.50.1.11/24 and node3 eth1=10.50.2.12/24 via nmcli, with static routes to the opposite /24 via node1
Confirmed lan-a/lan-b interface mapping empirically via ping before applying any firewall policy
Set up TCP listeners on node3 ports 5432 and 8080 (python2) as test targets, and opened tcp/5432 in node3's firewalld zone
Captured a fully-open baseline (ping and both ports reachable node2->node3) before adding router firewall rules
Applied VyOS ipv4 forward filter: default-action drop; rule 4 state established accept; rule 5 state related accept; rule 10 tcp dport 5432 iifname eth1 oifname eth2 accept
Verified node2->node3:5432 succeeds while ping, 8080, and node3->node2 traffic are all rejected
Captured baseline boot_id on all three nodes
Restarted node1 one at a time, polled until exec returned, confirmed changed boot_id, verified firewall rules/IPs/ip_forward persisted, re-verified node2->node3 traffic behavior
Restarted node2, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 IP/route/firewalld persisted, re-verified node2->node3 traffic behavior
Restarted node3, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 IP/firewalld persisted, restarted the test listener (killed by reboot), re-verified node2->node3 traffic behavior end-to-end

evidence.requirement: node2 (lan-a) can reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP/5432
evidence.summary: Baseline open connectivity, then post-firewall and post-all-three-restarts checks all show node2 successfully connecting to node3:5432 and receiving the test banner.

evidence.requirement: All other traffic between lan-a and lan-b is rejected
evidence.summary: Ping node2->node3, ping node3->node2, TCP/8080 node2->node3, and node3->node2:5432 all fail/timeout under the VyOS forward-filter policy, both before and after the restart cycle.

evidence.requirement: VyOS forward-filter firewall policy is correctly configured
evidence.summary: show firewall output on node1 confirms default-action drop, established/related accept rules, and the explicit tcp/5432 eth1->eth2 accept rule with correct match conditions.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline config captured (boot_id 5bcff8f9...), reboot acknowledged, post-boot boot_id is 193b977d... (changed), and firewall/interfaces/ip_forward all show the same committed config after restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 192f6cab... captured, reboot acknowledged, post-boot boot_id is 8376d9fe... (changed), and eth1 IP/route plus node2->node3 firewall behavior verified intact afterward.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ef457a88... captured, reboot acknowledged, post-boot boot_id is b7df436a... (changed), eth1 IP and firewalld port persisted, and end-to-end connectivity re-verified after restarting the killed test listener.
